### Load Libraries:

```{r}

library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(forcats)
library(janitor)
library(ggthemes)
library(PNWColors)

```


### Load in Data:

```{r}

intertidaldata <- read_csv(here("Week_09", "Data", "intertidaldata.csv"))

head(intertidaldata)

```

This dataset contains species abundance information in the form of percent cover and individual counts of some species (Whelks, Crabs, and Stars). First, the column titles need to be converted to a more R-friendly format.

---

### Cleaning Data Column Titles Using Janitor

```{r}

intertidaldata |> 
  clean_names() -> clean_intertidaldata

```

---

### Check the Data

```{r}

glimpse(clean_intertidaldata)

```


The column names look a lot better, but I can already see some errors in the intertidal data file. Let's get a summary of what's going on in there.

```{r}

clean_intertidaldata |> 
  count(quadrat, sort = TRUE)

```

OK so those two, "Low ." and "Mid 1" look like typos, so let's fix them.

```{r}

# I'm pretty sure there is a WAY better method to do this, but I couldn't figure it out :(

# pipe the dataframe in
clean_intertidaldata |> 
  
  # mutate the row to replace the problem value with the correct value
  mutate(quadrat = replace(clean_intertidaldata$quadrat, 
                           grep("Low  .", 
                                clean_intertidaldata$quadrat), 
                           "Low")) -> fixed_intertidaldata 
fixed_intertidaldata |> 
  # do the same thing with the other problem type 
  mutate(quadrat = replace(fixed_intertidaldata$quadrat,
                           grep("Mid  1",
                                fixed_intertidaldata$quadrat),
                           "Mid")) -> fixed_intertidaldata


# Now let's check the data:

fixed_intertidaldata |> 
  count(quadrat, sort = TRUE)

```

Much better!

Let's check the other categories as well:

```{r}

# check site
fixed_intertidaldata |> 
  count(site, sort = TRUE)

# check transect
fixed_intertidaldata |> 
  count(transect, sort = TRUE)



```

Both site and transect seem correct. Alright, let's factor!

---

### Factoring by Quadrat to Order the Levels:

```{r}

# mutate the quadrat column to be a factor with levels "low", "mid", and "high":
fixed_intertidaldata |> 
  mutate(quadrat = factor(quadrat, levels = c("Low", "Mid", "High"))) -> fixed_intertidaldata

glimpse(fixed_intertidaldata$quadrat)

```

Let's say I'm only interested in seeing the difference in percent cover of the three barnacle types at low, mid, and high quadrats. See code below for barnacle data selection and summarizing.

```{r}

fixed_intertidaldata |> 
  
  # keep only barnacles and site identifiers
  select(site, 
         transect, 
         quadrat, 
         small_barnacles, 
         large_barnacles, 
         gooseneck_barnacles) |> 
  
  # pivot longer 
  pivot_longer(cols = c(small_barnacles, large_barnacles, gooseneck_barnacles), 
               names_to = "barnacle_type", 
               values_to = "percent_cover") -> barnacles_data

# group_by and summarise the average percent cover into a separate variable
barnacles_data |> 
  group_by(site, quadrat, barnacle_type) |> 
  summarise(avg_percent_cover = mean(percent_cover)) -> barnacles_data_avg

glimpse(barnacles_data_avg)

```

Looks good. Now, let's plot.

---

### Plotting

```{r}
#| fig-align: center
#| label: fig-barnacles
#| fig-cap: "Average percent cover of each type of barnacle per site sampled. Average of 10 transects per quadrat. Cape Meares shows the highest proportion of large barnacles, while Starfish Point has an abundance of small barnacles at the High quadrat. Overall barnacles appear to be more common in the higher quadrats, with a few exceptions."
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 8

barnacles_data_avg |> 
  ggplot(mapping = aes(x = quadrat,
                       y = avg_percent_cover,               # base plot
                       color = fct_reorder2(barnacle_type, quadrat, barnacle_type), # reorder the legend
                       fill = barnacle_type)) +
  
  # make a column graph
  geom_col() +
  
  # facet wrap by site
  facet_wrap(~site) +
  
  # flip the coordinates to be more aesthetically pleasing
  coord_flip() +
  
  # add ylim as "100" was not showing
  ylim(0, 100) +
  
  # base theme
  theme_hc() +
  
  # edit some of the grid lines to be darker:
  theme(panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = "darkgray"),
        title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 18)) +
  
  # labels
  labs(title = "Intertidal Barnacle Cover",
       subtitle = "Average Percent Cover of Three Barnacle Types per Site",
       x = "Quadrat Tide Height",
       y = "Average Percent Cover",
       fill = "Barnacle Type:") +
  
  # add pretty colors and more lables
  scale_fill_manual(values = pnw_palette("Starfish", n = 3),
                    labels = c("Gooseneck Barnacles", "Large Barnacles", "Small Barnacles")) +
  
  # this helps separate out the colors above
  scale_color_manual(values = c("white", "white", "white")) +
  
  # remove color legend
  guides(color = "none")

```
